reasoning_summary:
Step-by-step verification of every numbered line.

0001: States the plan is to demonstrate the result for n = 118. As a statement of intent it is fine, but note the theorem is universally quantified over all integers n >= 118; verifying a single value cannot discharge it. This is the seed of the fatal gap recorded at the end.
0002, 0004, 0006: Blank formatting lines; nothing to justify.
0003: 4*118/3 = 472/3 = 157.333..., correct.
0005: The primes strictly between 118 and 157.33 are 127, 131, 137, 139, 149, 151, 157 (119=7*17, 121=11^2, 123=3*41, 125=5^3, 129=3*43, 133=7*19, 135, 141=3*47, 143=11*13, 145=5*29, 147=3*49, 153, 155 are all composite). The line's enumeration is therefore complete and correct.
0007 / 0050: begin-eqn / end-eqn delimiters; no content.
0008-0009: 4*32 - 1 = 128 - 1 = 127. Correct.
0010, 0013, 0016, 0019, 0022, 0025, 0028, 0031, 0034, 0037, 0040, 0043, 0046, 0049: eqn-block closing braces; no content.
0011-0012: 6*21 + 1 = 126 + 1 = 127. Correct.
0014-0015: 4*33 - 1 = 132 - 1 = 131. Correct.
0017-0018: 6*22 - 1 = 132 - 1 = 131. Correct.
0020-0021: 4*34 + 1 = 136 + 1 = 137. Correct.
0023-0024: 6*23 - 1 = 138 - 1 = 137. Correct.
0026-0027: 4*35 - 1 = 140 - 1 = 139. Correct.
0029-0030: 6*23 + 1 = 138 + 1 = 139. Correct.
0032-0033: 4*37 + 1 = 148 + 1 = 149. Correct.
0035-0036: 6*25 - 1 = 150 - 1 = 149. Correct.
0038-0039: 4*38 - 1 = 152 - 1 = 151. Correct.
0041-0042: 6*25 + 1 = 150 + 1 = 151. Correct.
0044-0045: 4*39 + 1 = 156 + 1 = 157. Correct.
0047-0048: 6*26 + 1 = 156 + 1 = 157. Correct.
0051, 0053, 0056, 0059, 0062, 0065, 0067, 0069, 0071, 0073, 0075: Blank formatting lines; nothing to justify.
0052: Transitional remark introducing the classification; unobjectionable.
0054-0055: Primes of the form 4m - 1 in the range: 127, 131, 139, 151. Each is 3 mod 4 (127=4*32-1, 131=4*33-1, 139=4*35-1, 151=4*38-1) and no other listed prime is; correct and consistent with lines 0008-0045.
0057-0058: FIRST FAILING STEP. Claims the primes of the form 4m + 1 are 137, 139, 157. This is false: 139 = 4*35 - 1 is 3 mod 4, as the proof's own line 0027 states, so 139 cannot also be of the form 4m + 1. The correct list is 137, 149, 157 (149 = 4*37 + 1 per line 0033, and 149 is omitted here). The line is internally contradictory with lines 0026-0027 and 0032-0033. The error is not fatal to the n = 118 case, since 137 and 157 already witness the 4m + 1 form, but the step as written is unjustified and false.
0060-0061: Primes of the form 6m - 1 in the range: 131, 137, 149. Each is 5 mod 6 (131=6*22-1, 137=6*23-1, 149=6*25-1) and the others are not; correct.
0063-0064: Primes of the form 6m + 1: 127, 139, 151, 157. Each is 1 mod 6 (127=6*21+1, 139=6*23+1, 151=6*25+1, 157=6*26+1); correct.
0066: Concludes the four conditions hold for n = 118. This follows from 0054-0064 (and would still follow after correcting 0058), so the single instance n = 118 is genuinely established.
0068: Transitional remark; nothing to justify.
0070: 4*117/3 = 468/3 = 156. Correct.
0072: Claims the primes between 117 and 157 are those between 118 and 157 excluding 157. Loosely worded (the relevant interval for n = 117 is (117, 156], and the point is that no prime lies in (117, 118)), but the substantive content is correct: the admissible primes for n = 117 are 127, 131, 137, 139, 149, 151.
0074: Concludes the conditions hold for n = 117. Checking the reduced list: 4m - 1 gives 127, 131, 139, 151; 4m + 1 gives 137 and 149; 6m - 1 gives 131, 137, 149; 6m + 1 gives 127, 139, 151. All four forms are represented, so the claim is true. Note, however, that if one had relied on the erroneous list of line 0058, the 4m + 1 witnesses after deleting 157 would have been recorded as 137, 139, only one of which is genuine, so the step is true but its stated support is contaminated by the 0058 error.
0076: An editorial aside questioning the hypothesis n >= 118. Not a mathematical step and it contributes nothing toward the theorem.

Overall: besides the concrete false statement at 0058, the argument is fatally incomplete as a proof of the stated theorem. The theorem asserts that for EVERY integer n >= 118 the interval (n, 4n/3) contains a prime of each of the four forms; the proof only exhibits the interval for the single value n = 118 (plus the extra case n = 117) and never treats general n. No induction, no Bertrand-type or Dirichlet-type density input, and no covering argument linking successive intervals appears anywhere. Hence the universally quantified conclusion is never derived, and the write-up ends with a meta-comment rather than a proof.
